faq.q: Why is my AC blowing warm air?
faq.a: Common causes include a dirty air filter, low refrigerant from a leak, a failed capacitor or compressor, or a thermostat setting. Refrigerant is regulated, so low refrigerant needs a certified technician rather than a top-off from a kit.

faq.q: Should I keep running an AC that has ice on it?
faq.a: No. Turn the system off and let the ice melt. Running it while frozen can damage the compressor. Then call a technician to find out why it froze.

faq.q: How often should I change my air filter?
faq.a: Many manufacturers suggest every one to three months, depending on the filter type, pets, and dust. A clogged filter is one of the most common causes of poor cooling.

faq.q: How long does an air conditioner last?
faq.a: Often 10 to 15 years, and heavy use in a hot climate can shorten that. Age, repair history, and efficiency all matter when deciding between repair and replacement.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a new AC?
faq.a: Many cities require a permit for replacing an air conditioner. A licensed contractor normally handles it. Ask {business} what applies in {city}.

faq.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
faq.a: Leave the home right away, do not use switches or phones inside, and call your gas utility or 911 from outside. Do not try to repair it yourself.

faq.q: Why will my furnace not ignite?
faq.a: Common causes are a dirty flame sensor, a failed igniter, a gas supply problem, or a control board fault. A technician tests each safely.

faq.q: How often should a furnace be serviced?
faq.a: Annual service is commonly recommended before the heating season to check safety controls and airflow.

faq.q: What is the difference between a furnace and a heat pump?
faq.a: A furnace burns fuel or uses electric resistance to make heat. A heat pump moves heat and can also cool. Which fits depends on your climate, existing equipment, and utility costs.

faq.q: How long does a furnace last?
faq.a: Often 15 to 20 years with regular maintenance, though it varies by model and use.

faq.q: Can I replace only the furnace?
faq.a: Sometimes. Matching the outdoor unit, coil, and ductwork affects performance, so a technician should assess the whole system.

faq.q: What does an HVAC tune-up include?
faq.a: Typically filter, coils, electrical connections, capacitor, refrigerant check, drain line, and thermostat operation. Ask exactly what your technician covers.

faq.q: How often should I service my system?
faq.a: Once a year is commonly recommended, ideally before the season when you use it most.

faq.q: Will a tune-up lower my bills?
faq.a: A clean, well-adjusted system runs more efficiently, but savings depend on the system's condition. It also reduces the chance of a breakdown.

faq.q: What counts as an HVAC emergency?
faq.a: No cooling during dangerous heat, no heat in freezing weather, burning smells, smoke, or water leaking from the unit. Elderly people, infants, and pets are at higher risk.

faq.q: What should I do while I wait for a technician?
faq.a: Turn the system off if there is a burning smell or leak, keep the home as cool or warm as you can, and stay hydrated in heat.
